extracted.intended_audience: Personnel assigned or preparing to serve as Public Information Officer; Assistant Public Information Officers; Incident Management Team members; public- or private-sector emergency responders working within ICS environments.
extracted.subtask_description: A four-day course preparing personnel to serve as Public Information Officers on an Incident Management Team, teaching incident communications, media relations, information management, coordination with Command Staff/partner agencies, and practical skills via scenario-based exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary PIO role and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Information Officer (PIO) serves as the primary point of contact between the Incident Management Team and the public, media, and partner agencies, ensuring timely, accurate, and coordinated information throughout incident operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PIO is a member of the Command Staff and must manage communications to support situational awareness; criteria include being timely, accurate, coordinated, and maintaining liaison with media and partner agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the PIO role during incident operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the role and importance of the Public Information Officer during incident operations, including initial response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should assess whether the candidate can articulate PIO objectives across phases of response (including initial response), how PIO actions affect operations and public safety, and how the PIO integrates with Command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information management fundamentals and workspace setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the fundamentals of information management and how to establish the PIO staff and workspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes organizing information flows, tracking public inquiries/media contacts, setting up a PIO workspace/staff structure, documentation practices, and tools/processes to ensure accurate, auditable information dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing an effective communications strategy and media plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an effective communications strategy and media plan for sharing incident information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion covers ability to identify audiences, key messages, channels/timing, approval pathways, coordination needs, contingencies, and measurable objectives for outreach; practical exercises (planning activities) are used to demonstrate competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations and social media best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate best practices for media relations, including social media engagement and problem-solving during incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should include conducting media briefings, preparing spokespeople, crafting clear messages, using social media appropriately, monitoring/mitigating misinformation, and demonstrating problem-solving under pressure (role-play/media briefing exercises).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant PIO roles and relationship to PIO
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the roles and responsibilities of Assistant Public Information Officers and their relationship to the PIO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators look for clarity on delegation, tasking, supervisory relationships, handoffs, and coordination between PIO and assistant staff to ensure consistent messaging and operational efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with Incident Management Team and partner agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how to build and maintain effective relationships with the Incident Management Team and participate in meetings and briefings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes demonstrating regular participation in IMT briefings, information-sharing protocols with Command Staff and partner agencies, joint messaging, and mechanisms to resolve information conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community relations during an incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe steps for establishing and maintaining community relations during an incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers outreach to affected communities, public trust-building, culturally appropriate messaging, local stakeholder engagement, and strategies to address public concerns and questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing special public information situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply appropriate actions for managing special situations involving public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes responding to high-profile incidents, fatalities, legal/sensitive issues, rumors and misinformation, and other atypical scenarios; assessment via problem-solving exercises and scenario-based role plays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety considerations for PIOs and escorts
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe safety considerations for PIOs and those they escort or work with in the incident environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate knowledge of scene safety, protective equipment, movement/restriction protocols, and procedures for escorting media or visitors while maintaining safety and operational security.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO responsibilities during transition and demobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline the PIO’s responsibilities during incident transition and demobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes final public messaging, transfer of information to recovery/public affairs, documentation/recordkeeping, release of after-action materials, and ensuring continuity of communications as operations scale down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating PIO effectiveness and applying lessons learned
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate PIO effectiveness and apply lessons learned through exercise components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment involves after-action reviews, performance metrics, identifying improvement actions, incorporating lessons into plans and training, and demonstrating iterative improvement based on exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation in ICS principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Course builds on ICS fundamentals and focuses on the PIO’s duties and responsibilities, including incident communications, media relations, and coordination with Command Staff and partner agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should demonstrate familiarity with ICS structure and principles as they apply to the PIO role (e.g., chain of command, unity of effort, information flow). Successful completion of ICS-300 is recommended as a prerequisite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and instructional methods (scenario-based/role-play)
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities may include instructor-led, in-person training supported by realistic scenario-based learning, group discussion and facilitated instruction, media briefings and role-play exercises, incident communication planning activities, problem-solving exercises, and asynchronous activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of realistic scenarios, role-plays, and media-briefing exercises is expected to demonstrate applied competence; evaluation should consider performance in exercises as evidence of skill, not only classroom knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite and course alignment notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended Pre-requisite: Successful completion of ICS-300. Note: This course aligns with FEMA’s National Preparedness Course Catalog for the NIMS ICS All-Hazards Public Information Officer (0952) but is not an official FEMA course and does not confer FEMA certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations/AHJs should confirm prerequisite requirements; course alignment indicates conformity to recognized standards though it does not replace formal FEMA certification—this affects credential expectations.
